result.releaseSummary: This release introduces a floating animated agent companion UI with Launch, Activate/Deactivate, hover reactions, and scoped OpenAI chat for Admin and assigned Editor users. It adds per-user companion preferences (persisted in a new store), strict agent access control, and robust session/role validation at every async boundary. No tool execution or publishing is enabled. The API and store logic are covered by focused unit and regression tests, including role demotion and access revocation scenarios. All TypeScript, lint, build, and gate tests pass. Real OpenAI conversational flow, UI, and preferences persistence are verified on desktop. No database or environment changes. Rollback is a feature revert.
changedAreas: Data store: companion preferences (new Netlify/local store)
UI: floating agent companion (not included in supplied files, but referenced in release summary)
Auth/session: requireUser, role checks, session expiry
OpenAI API: conversational chat (no tool execution)
Testing: new/updated unit and regression tests
risks: {"area":"Mobile/responsive UI","severity":"medium","description":"Physical mobile devices remain untested. Only browser responsive checks at 480px+ are confirmed. There is no evidence of real device or touch interaction testing for the floating companion UI."}

{"area":"Agent access control","severity":"medium","description":"While regression tests cover demotion and scope changes, the companionData and canAccessAgent logic is complex and could have edge cases if agent scopes or user roles are updated concurrently. No explicit concurrency or race condition tests are shown."}

{"area":"Preferences store isolation","severity":"low","description":"Tests confirm preferences cannot overwrite credentials or other users, but there is no evidence of concurrent preference writes or reads under high load."}

{"area":"OpenAI API error handling","severity":"low","description":"Provider failures are handled and tested, but there is a risk of partial saves or user confusion if OpenAI is intermittently unavailable."}

{"area":"UI/UX: Floating companion","severity":"low","description":"No UI code or screenshots are included in the supplied files. The summary references a screenshot, but actual UI/UX edge cases (focus, keyboard, accessibility, animation reduce-motion) are not evidenced."}
smokeTests: GET /api/agents/companion as Admin returns agent data and preferences
POST /api/agents/companion with action: 'talk' as Admin returns OpenAI reply, agents remain Paused
POST /api/agents/companion with action: 'preferences' saves and returns updated preferences
Provider failure returns 502 with messageSaved: true
regressionTests: Role revocation at each async boundary blocks access and never leaks admin data
Preferences cannot overwrite credentials, roles, or other users
Missing or inactive users are rejected for preferences read/write
Agent access is filtered by canAccessAgent and user scopes
No tool execution or publishing is possible via companion API
edgeCases: Session expiry or HMAC invalidation during multi-step POST
Editor demoted to viewer during request
Admin demoted to editor with reduced scope during request
Preferences store file missing (ENOENT) returns undefined
Concurrent preference writes (not tested, see risk)
adminChecks: Admin can access all agents and preferences
Editor can only access assigned agents (Bob, Fiddle) and only if scoped
Viewer cannot access companion API at all
No admin data is leaked to editors after demotion
thirdPartyChecks: OpenAI API is only called if openaiConfigured is true
Provider errors are handled and surfaced to user

rollbackSteps: Restore previous /api/agents/companion API and agent store logic

testResults: All unit and regression tests pass (gate406 tests, 1 skip)
Desktop UI and preferences persistence confirmed
Cross-origin, private agent, execution action, demoted viewer session all return correct errors

result.cursorFixPrompt: 1. Provide evidence of physical mobile device testing for the floating agent companion UI, including touch interaction and responsive layout. 2. Supply at least one screenshot or video of the floating companion UI in use on a real mobile device. 3. Optionally, add a concurrency test for simultaneous preference writes/reads to the companion preferences store to confirm isolation under load. 4. If UI code is included in a separate PR, reference it and ensure accessibility and reduce-motion settings are tested. Once these are addressed, re-submit for review.
